11.1.3 Microbiological panel — the four Aspergillus species (verbatim substance, secondary)

Secondary summary (Morning Ag Clips, accessed 2026-11-01): “The microbiological contaminant compliance testing looks specifically for Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli, Salmonella species, and four pathogenic species of Aspergillus: Aspergillus flavus, A. fumigatus, A. niger and A. terreus. The current requirements for Aspergillus testing is not a general Aspergillus test. The rules for microbiological contaminant testing may be found under OAR 333-007-0390” — https://www.morningagclips.com/microbiological-contaminant-testing-update/ — secondary, accessed 2026-11-01. “The testing rules require a laboratory to use a molecular approach such as qPCR or other technologies that can detect sequences of DNA specific to the four species” — same source. OAR 333-007-0390 text itself was not opened in this run — Verify the panel, the qPCR requirement, and the effective dates against the current rule before quoting as law. The addition was recommended by a 2019 Secretary of State audit (same secondary source).

11.1.4 Sampling rules — who samples, how, and what must be present

  • Only laboratory personnel sample. This is the structural rule of OAR 333-007-0360/0370 and ORELAP-SOP-001/002 (see below). The 2026 enforcement cases turn on it: a producer may not hand the sampler extra material, and the sampler may not accept it.
  • Entire batch must be available. Cold Frame settlement charges (secondary reporting of OLCC charges, Cannabis News, accessed 2026-11-01): on 7 Nov, 27 Nov and 15 Dec 2023 Cold Frame “did not make an entire batch of marijuana available for sampling by Reference Labs, as Oregon Health Authority rule OAR 333-007-0360(1)(d) requires” — https://www.cannabisnews.org/united-states-cannabis-news/oregon-olcc-cold-frame-kief-lab-samples-thc-potency-license-surrender/ — secondary, accessed 2026-11-01. The OLCC synopsis: the company “failed to have an entire batch present during sampling making the sample not representative of the batch” — same source.
  • Representative sample. OAR 333-064-0100 (permanent order PH 14-2026, eff. 20 Jan 2026, search result, accessed 2026-11-01): a lab’s sampling policies/procedures, accredited by ORELAP, must “(A) Ensure sampling will result in a sample that is representative of the batch being sampled” and “(C) Require chain of custody procedures consistent with TNI EL Standard V1M2 5.7 and 5.8” — https://stage.oregon.gov/oha/PH/LABORATORYSERVICES/ENVIRONMENTALLABORATORYACCREDITATION/Documents/PH_14-2026TrackedChanges.pdf — accessed 2026-11-01 (permanent order filing, not the rule page itself — Verify against SOS OAR page).
  • Incorporated sampling protocols (current as of PH 14-2026, eff. 20 Jan 2026): “(i) Usable Marijuana: ORELAP-SOP-001 Rev 4.1; and (ii) Concentrates, Extracts, Products, and Industrial Hempderived Vapor Items: ORELAP-SOP-002 Rev 4.3” — same permanent order. Plus “Exhibit C, Table 1: Accuracy requirements for laboratory control samples (LCS). No changes are being made to the rule text” in that order — same source. Earlier SOP revisions are superseded; do not cite Rev 4.0/4.2 SOPs as current.
  • Only the finished product is sampled where finished-product testing is required: OAR 333-064-0100(2)(F) (same permanent order): sampling procedures must “(F) Ensure that only the finished cannabinoid concentrate, extract, product, or industrial hempderived vapor item is sampled if testing on the finished … item is required under OAR 333-007-0330 and OAR 333-007-0340” — same source (paraphrase of the filed text; Verify against SOS page).
  • Batch-size note (secondary, NOT rule text): a non-Oregon COA-mapping site states Oregon “flower batches can reach 50 pounds” and “Only a lab employee may take the sample” — https://weed-central.com/learn/coa/ — secondary, accessed 2026-11-01. The 50-lb figure is NOT confirmed on an opened OAR page in this run — Verify against OAR 333-007-0310/0360 batch definitions (harvest lot / process lot / test batch) before quoting. Do not use it as a rule.
  • Pre-tested quarantine — OAR 845-025-5720 (search result, accessed 2026-11-01): “Following samples being taken from a harvest or process lot batch a licensee must: Label the batch with … The name and accreditation number of the laboratory that took samples and the name and accreditation number of the laboratory that will perform the testing, if different; The test batch or sample unique identification numbers supplied by the laboratory personnel; The date the samples were taken; and In bold, capital letters, no smaller than 12 point font, ‘PRODUCT NOT TESTED.’ Store and secure the batch in a manner that prevents the product from being tampered with or transferred or sold prior to test results being reported. If the samples pass testing the product may be sold or transferred … (4) If the samples do not pass testing the licensee must comply with OAR 845-025-5740 (Failed Test Samples) and 333-007-0450 (Failed Test Samples), as applicable.” — https://oregon.public.law/rules/oar_845-025-5720 — search-result rendering, accessed 2026-11-01. Snippet-derived — Verify against the official SOS OAR page (the search result itself cites https://secure.sos.state.or.us/oard/view.action?ruleNumber=845-025-5720, accessed 26 May 2025 in that rendering).
  • Who pays / who chooses the lab: OAR 845-025-5700(2)(e) (opened): “Producer licenses are responsible for testing fee and may choose any laboratory licensee to conduct the test.” — https://oregon.public.law/rules/oar_845-025-5700 — accessed 2026-11-01. (Wording “Producer licenses” is as rendered; read as producer licensees.)
  • Pesticide capacity exception — OAR 845-025-5700(2) (opened, full text in §11.1.1): if Commission staff finds insufficient lab capacity for pesticide testing, staff may order random-batch pesticide testing instead of every-batch testing; at least one batch of every harvest lot must be tested; if any randomly chosen sample fails, EVERY batch from that harvest lot must be tested; if all randomly chosen samples pass, the whole harvest lot is considered passed; staff must give 10 days’ notice before reverting to every-batch testing. Whether any such capacity order is in force as of 1 Nov 2026 is Unavailable in this run — do not assume every-batch pesticide testing is currently suspended or currently required on capacity grounds alone; the default rule is every-batch testing, and any capacity order must be checked on the OLCC site.

11.1.5 Failed tests, reanalysis, retesting, remediation, recalls, audit testing

  • 24-hour failure reporting (lab → agency, before grower/processor). OHA page (opened): “Failed test results must be reported to the overseeing state agency by the testing laboratory within 24 hours of completion of the laboratory’s data review and approval procedures and be reported at the same time or before reporting to the grower or processor.” — https://www.oregon.gov/OHA/PH/DiseasesConditions/ChronicDisease/MedicalMarijuanaProgram/Pages/testing.aspx — accessed 2026-11-01. “Additional information for reporting medical marijuana items that fail testing can be found under Laboratory Reporting Requirements” — same page.
  • Reanalysis (same lab, 7 days). OHA page (opened): “If a registrant or licensee who requests testing … receives a failed result, they may request a reanalysis of the sample from the same laboratory within seven days of being notified of the failure. If the reanalysis results in another fail, all associated batches must be held for destruction*. If the reanalysis results in a pass, then another laboratory must resample and retest the item” — same page. The OLCC failure-notification form (search result) states the same clocks in rule terms: “A request for reanalysis must be made to the lab within 7 days of the results being reported into the Cannabis Tracking System (CTS). The reanalysis must occur within 30 days of the date of this request.” — form summary, accessed 2026-11-01. Note the two triggers differ (notification vs CTS reporting) — the form’s CTS trigger is the operative rule formulation; the OHA page’s “notified” phrasing is guidance. Verify OAR 333-007-0450 for the controlling trigger.
  • Retesting (second lab, 30 days, no common ownership, no original subcontractor). OHA page (opened): “Retesting must be completed by a second laboratory within 30 days from the date the retesting was requested. Retesting may not be performed at a laboratory under the same ownership as the original laboratory that performed the original testing and may not be done by a laboratory that was subcontracted to do the original testing. A fail on a retest means the item must be held for destruction*. A pass on a retest means the item may be transferred.” — same page. Form summary: “the licensee may then have another laboratory resample the batch and confirm the passing result. The request for retesting must be made within 7 days of the results being reported into CTS. Retesting must occur within 30 days of the date of this request.” — form, accessed 2026-11-01.
  • Notification duty on reanalysis/retesting requests. Form summary: “The licensee is required by OAR 333-007-0450 to notify the Commission of a request for reanalysis, retesting, and all results from reanalysis and retesting.” — form, accessed 2026-11-01. For medical registrants, OHA page (opened): the grower/processor must notify OMMP on the Notification of Reanalysis or Retesting of a Failed Sample Form, and submit a copy of the reanalysis/retesting results to OMMP once received; “If a batch fails testing, it may not be destroyed without first obtaining permission from OMMP.” — same page. Form/results may be sent to ommp.labs@odhsoha.oregon.gov as stated on the OHA page (agency public contact — reproduced as stated on the official page).
  • Remediation — only where OAR 333-007-0450 allows it. OHA page (opened): “An option to remediate the batch may be possible before destruction. Please consult OAR 333-007-0450 to determine if remediation is possible for the item and test that failed.” — same page. Form summary: “Some marijuana items may be eligible for reanalysis and remediation. See OAR 333-007-0450 to determine if a sample is eligible for possible reanalysis.” and “Batches of these items that fail the required tests and that are not reanalysed or remediated as allowed by OAR 333-007-0450 must be held by the licensee until they are destroyed in a manner approved by the Commission.” — form, accessed 2026-11-01. The eligible item/test matrix in 333-007-0450 was NOT opened in this run (rate-limit) — Verify the matrix before advising any remediation. In particular, pesticide/solvent failures have a distinct destruction-approval track (see below) and must not be assumed remediable.
  • Pesticide/solvent failure destruction approval. Form summary: “If a passing pesticide result is not confirmed or a licensee chooses not to have the laboratory reanalyse the sample, then OAR 333-007-0450 requires that the licensee destroy the batch in a manner approved by the Commission.” / “The Commission must approve the destruction of any marijuana item that failed pesticide or solvent testing, and did not undergo or pass subsequent reanalysis or retesting.” / “You may elect to either (1) surrender the failed marijuana item to Commission staff, who will arrange for the item’s destruction, or (2) destroy [it in the approved manner] … You must destroy items only in the approved [manner] … may not destroy the items until directed” — form, accessed 2026-11-01. Form-derived — Verify against OAR 333-007-0450 / 845-025-5740 text.
  • Failed-test rule citation (OLCC side): OAR 845-025-5740 (Failed Test Samples) is the OLCC companion to OAR 333-007-0450; OAR 845-025-5720(4) cross-refers to both (see §11.1.4). The full 5740 text was not opened — Verify.
  • Recalls — what was located, and what was not. No standalone Oregon cannabis recall rule (OAR 845-025-xxxx recall procedure, recall classification, or OLCC recall-order authority) was confirmed on an opened official page in this run. What IS established: (a) failed batches are held, not sold, under 5720/5740/333-007-0450; (b) OLCC may require audit/compliance testing and, for potency audit testing on/after 1 Dec 2022, may order relabelling to the audit mean where the difference is statistically significant at 99% (OAR 845-025-5760(4), search result — see §11.1.6); (c) OLCC enforcement (suspension/cancellation, §11.2.7) can remove product/licensees from the market. A general “OLCC recall” procedure, if it exists in rule or in a compliance bulletin, is Unavailable in this run — Verify on the OLCC compliance/recall pages before stating any recall duty, timeline, or consumer-notification rule. Do not import other states’ recall rules.
  • Control studies / R&D testing: OAR 333-007-0310 defines “Control study” as “a study performed on products or matrices of unknown homogeneity to assure required uniformity of product accomplished through sampling and testing as described in OAR 333-007-0440 (Control Study)” — search result, https://oregon.public.law/rules/oar_333-007-0310 — accessed 2026-11-01. The 0440 procedure and the quality-control/R&D testing rules (333-007-0500) were not opened — Verify.

11.1.6 Audit, compliance and random testing; lab accreditation; licensed-lab list

  • OLCC audit testing — OAR 845-025-5760 (search result, accessed 2026-11-01): “(1) The Commission may require a licensee or laboratory licensee to submit samples identified by the Commission to one or more laboratories of the Commission’s choosing to be tested in order to determine whether a licensee is in compliance with the cannabis testing rules found in OAR chapter 333, division 7 or any other rules of the Commission and may require additional testing that is not required by these rules. (2) A laboratory doing audit testing must comply with these rules … and if conducting testing not required by these rules, may only use Authority approved methods, unless otherwise authorized by the Commission. (3) The Commission may, at any time, require a licensee or laboratory licensee to permit the sampling of or submit a sample … to the Commission for testing. Such testing may include testing for: (a) Anything that is required to be tested under OAR chapter 333, division 7 … (b) Any microbiological contaminant. (c) Heavy metals. (d) Other adulterants, pesticides, solvents, additives, or contaminants that may pose a risk to public health and safety, or are prohibited by law. (4) When audit testing for potency pursuant to this rule, the Commission may require any portion of a batch with a compliance test for potency on or after December 1, 2022, to be relabeled with the mean average result from laboratories conducting audit testing if the Commission determines that there is a statistically significant difference at a 99 percent confidence interval between the audit testing result … and the original compliance testing result … (a) … Shapiro-Wilk test … at a 95 percent confidence interval. (b) … one-sample Student’s t-test … (c) … one-sample Wilcoxon Signed-Rank test … (5) A licensee shall submit all samples required for testing under this rule within a timeframe established by the Commission. (6) Violations. Failure to submit requested samples to OLCC … is a Category II violation.” — https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/oregon/Or-Admin-Code-SS-845-025-5760 — search-result rendering of the Cornell LII mirror, accessed 2026-11-01. Snippet-derived — Verify against the SOS OAR page. The 1 Dec 2022 potency-audit cut-off and the statistical tests are as rendered; do not paraphrase them away.
  • Secondary-lab Metrc entry (CE2026-01, eff. 1 Sep 2026): primary lab records all compliance results under primary samples; secondary lab records only “Composite Testing Complete” on the composite sample; failure after 1 Sep 2026 “will result in missing test results for the source package” (Run 1 §1.7, OLCC bulletin https://www.oregon.gov/olcc/marijuana/Pages/CE2026-01.aspx). The bulletin “does not supersede any OLCC rule.”
  • ORELAP accreditation — standard, scope, location rule. OHA ORELAP cannabis page (search result, accessed 2026-11-01): “ORELAP accredits cannabis testing under ORS 475C.540 to 475C.590. Laboratories are accredited to the TNI Standards and are held accountable to the rules found in [OAR] Chapter 333, Division 64. Currently, laboratories must be located in Oregon to be accredited for cannabis testing.” — https://www.oregon.gov/oha/PH/LaboratoryServices/EnvironmentalLaboratoryAccreditation/Pages/cannabis-info.aspx — accessed 2026-11-01. Note: the page as rendered still cites the ORS range in 475C form (good); the TNI standard is the 2016 TNI Standard (secondary lab-accreditation summary, accessed 2026-11-01: laboratories must “Purchase the Nelac Institute (TNI) 2016 Standard” — https://oregonstatecannabis.org/licensing/testing — secondary).
  • Division 64 permanent changes, 23 July 2024 (OHA ORELAP page, search result): “Requires mycotoxin biological tissue proficiency test (PT) samples to be in usable marijuana matrix (effective August 1, 2024)”; “Adds a requirement that laboratories obtain and maintain a license from Oregon Psilocybin Services (OPS) for psilocybin testing laboratories and the [OLCC] for cannabis testing laboratories as criteria for maintaining ORELAP accreditation”; “Clarifies testing of pre-roll joints”; “Sets minimum sample material retention for thirty (30) days for cannabis testing laboratories”; “Details on how to report PT results, including maximum limit of quantitation (LOQ) for PTs based on existing LOQs for compliance samples” — same ORELAP page, accessed 2026-11-01.
  • Division 64 sampling-protocol update, PH 14-2026 eff. 20 Jan 2026: amends OAR 333-064-0100, reattaching ORELAP-SOP-001 Rev 4.1, ORELAP-SOP-002 Rev 4.3, and Exhibit C Table 1 (LCS accuracy); repeals temporary 333-064-0100 from PH 18-2025; “No changes are being made to the rule text” in that order — permanent order filing, https://stage.oregon.gov/oha/PH/LABORATORYSERVICES/ENVIRONMENTALLABORATORYACCREDITATION/Documents/PH_14-2026TrackedChanges.pdf — accessed 2026-11-01.
  • OLCC lab licence — OAR 845-025-5030 (opened directly 2026-11-01), verbatim substance: “(1)(a) A laboratory that intends to collect samples or test marijuana items for producer, processor, wholesale, or retail licensees, or research certificate holders must be licensed by the Commission. (b) An applicant … must comply with … OAR 845-025-1030 (Application Process) and pay the required application and license fees. (d) … the Commission may refuse to issue a laboratory license for any violation [of] ORS 475B.550 [now 475C.540] to 475B.590 [now 475C.590], OAR 333-007-0300 to 333-007-0490, OAR 333, Division 64 or these rules. (e) … the Commission may refuse to issue a laboratory license to any person who: (A) Holds a producer, processor, wholesale or retail license; (B) Is registered with the authority under ORS 475B.420 [now 475C.792 grow-site registration] and is a person designated to produce marijuana by a registry identification cardholder …; or (C) Is registered with the authority under ORS 475B.435 or 475B.450 [medical processing-site/dispensary registration]. (g) A laboratory that is only accredited to perform sampling may be designated as a Sampling Laboratory for purposes of the licensing fee in OAR 845-025-1060 (Fees). This designation may only be changed upon license renewal. (2)(a) … an applicant for a laboratory license must be accredited by the Authority under OAR 333, Division 64 for any cannabis sampling or testing the applicant will perform … (b) An applicant … may apply for licensure prior to receiving accreditation, but the Commission will not issue a license until proof of accreditation is received. (d) … the Commission may consider an application incomplete if the applicant does not obtain accreditation … within six months of applying for a license. … An applicant whose application is declared incomplete may reapply at any time. (e) A licensed laboratory must maintain accreditation … at all times while licensed … If a laboratory’s accreditation lapses or is revoked … the laboratory may not perform any activities that are subject to the lapsed or revoked accreditation until it is reinstated. (f) Exercising license privileges without proper accreditation is a Category I violation and could result in license revocation. (3)(a) A laboratory must renew its license annually … in accordance with OAR 845-025-1190 (License Renewal).” — https://oregon.public.law/rules/oar_845-025-5030 — opened 2026-11-01.   • Licensed-lab list — how to get it, and why this draft does NOT print a lab roster. The authoritative list is the OLCC Marijuana Businesses and Endorsements dataset on the Oregon Open Data Portal (Socrata dataset ID q32u-cmam, updated 28 Sep 2026 per CannBus — Run 1 Part 5 §5.1; direct download link NOT located verbatim in Run 1 — Verify on data.oregon.gov) plus the OLCC interactive Map of Recreational Marijuana Retailers & Labs (OLCC marijuana page, https://www.oregon.gov/olcc/marijuana/pages/default.aspx — search result, accessed 2026-11-01) and the ORELAP accredited-lab list (OHA ORELAP Laboratories page, linked from the OHA testing page). A named roster printed here would be stale on publication: labs were under active OLCC sanction in Sep–Oct 2026 (see §11.1.7), and accreditation scope varies by test (see below). The dataset + ORELAP list are the sources; any roster must be pulled on the date of use.
  • CONFLICT — lab counts (do not resolve by picking one): (a) Late Sep 2026 OLCC dataset (CannBus Q3 2026, secondary tabulation, accessed 2026-11-01): 9 laboratories active (10 active lab rows for 9 licence numbers) — https://www.cannbus.org/cannmir/or_cannmir.html. (b) Secondary lab-licensing summary (accessed 2026-11-01): “As of April 2025, there are 12 ORELAP accredited testing cannabis laboratories in Oregon. However, only five of these facilities are accredited to conduct all the tests required by OMMP” — https://oregonstatecannabis.org/licensing/testing — secondary, Apr 2025. (c) CannBus note: “a trade-law roundup counts 10 labs, down from 11 after the 2024 THC-inflation crackdown” — same CannBus page. These differ by date (Apr 2025 vs Sep 2026), by universe (ORELAP accreditation vs OLCC licence vs trade roundup), and by scope (accredited for some tests vs all tests). The 5-of-12 “all tests” point matters operationally: a lab accredited for potency only cannot clear a batch for sale. Verify scope on the ORELAP list before engaging a lab.
  • One named lab, as an example only (public business listing, not a roster): Rose City Laboratories, 7200 SE Johnson Creek Blvd., Portland, OR 97206 — OLCC Licensed Laboratory #1002112892C, ORELAP Accredited Environmental Testing Laboratory #4096 (lab’s own site, accessed 2026-11-01: https://www.rosecitylabs.com/mobile-asbestos-lab-copy and https://www.rosecitylabs.com/hemp-cannabis). Licence/accreditation numbers are public business identifiers as published by the lab itself; Verify current status on the OLCC dataset / ORELAP list before relying on them — Sep–Oct 2026 sanctions touched other labs and status may have changed.

11.1.7 2026 sampling-fraud enforcement (context for §§11.1.4–11.1.5)

  • 25 Sep 2026: OLCC sent notices to seven licensed testing laboratories, proposing cancellation in some cases and suspension/fines in others, for sampling failures (batch not fully available; too few increments) and, for three labs, intentional addition of kief/concentrate to samples — Category I violations, default sanction revocation (Run 1 H5; secondary reporting: Harris Sliwoski, https://harris-sliwoski.com/cannalawblog/oregon-cracks-down-on-thc-inflation-and-testing-labs/ — accessed 2026-11-01). The individual lab names and the final dispositions (cancelled vs suspended vs settled) were not extracted in this run — Verify on the OLCC stipulated-settlement / commission-order pages before naming any lab as sanctioned.
  • Cold Frame, LLC (Washington County, producer licence 10078868202): settlement dated 15 Oct 2026 — admitted supplying kief to Reference Labs samples on 7 Nov, 27 Nov and 15 Dec 2023; charged under OAR 845-025-8540(2)(a)(C) (intentionally/knowingly misrepresenting potency — Category I) and OAR 333-007-0360(1)(d) (entire batch not available); accepted a Letter of Reprimand and agreed to surrender its licence by 7 a.m. 13 Jan 2027 unless a pending change-of-ownership is approved (Run 1 H5; secondary: https://www.cannabisnews.org/united-states-cannabis-news/oregon-olcc-cold-frame-kief-lab-samples-thc-potency-license-surrender/ — accessed 2026-11-01). A parallel March 2026 settlement (Nebadon, Inc., kief added before PREE Laboratories sampling, 10 Nov 2023) is reported in the same secondary article — Verify on the OLCC settlement pages; do not quote the Nebadon terms from secondary alone.
  • Operational consequence: sampling integrity is now the highest-enforcement-risk operations area in Oregon. Licensees should assume OLCC will audit-test potency (OAR 845-025-5760) and compare audit vs compliance results at 99% confidence.

11.1.8 Hemp testing (operations cross-reference; full treatment is Part 7)

  • ODA hemp programme: pre-harvest total-THC testing under the USDA-approved Oregon state plan (approved Jan 2022 per Run 1 §4.8, secondary — Verify on USDA AMS list). Oregon total THC = (delta-9-THCA × 0.877) + delta-9-THC (Run 1 H8). Federal baseline: USDA DEA-registered-lab enforcement delayed to 31 Dec 2026; PL 119-37 §781 eff. 12 Nov 2026, limited until 11 Dec 2026, then total-THC + 0.4 mg/container cap — whether Oregon’s 0.877 factor and ODA lab rules conform after 11 Dec 2026 is Verify; as of 1 Nov 2026 ODA stated Oregon would “continue operating under current Oregon laws and rules, including Oregon’s existing definition of total THC” during transition (ODA GovDelivery bulletin, https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/ORODA/bulletins/3fc8e8e — Run 1 H8).
  • Hemp-derived vapor items and cannabinoid hemp products for consumers: OAR 333 Div. 7 testing (OHA page scope, opened) + OLCC Hemp Registry registration from 1 Jan 2026, enforcement from 1 June 2026, complaint-driven/education-first (Run 1 H6). Consumer-accessible test results are a Registry requirement, not just a lab COA.
  • Hemp lab accreditation: ODA-registered hemp testing laboratories (distinct from OLCC labs) — the ODA hemp-testing-lab register was not opened in this run — Verify on ODA hemp pages.

11.2 Licence rules — transfers, ownership, renewal, caps, relocation, surrender, revocation, insurance/bonding

11.2.1 Transfers and sales; change of ownership; change of financial interest / business structure

  • The live entry route. Because HB 4121 caps close new producer/processor/wholesaler/retailer applications (Run 1 §4.9), entry is by buying an existing licence and filing a change-of-ownership application in CAMP (https://camp.olcc.online/), with OLCC processing changes from the 20 Oct 2026 assignment date noted in Run 1 §4.9. OLCC’s licensed-businesses page states: “New Applications for Producer, Processors, Wholesalers, and Retailers are not being accepted at this time. ‘Marijuana License Caps and Moratorium,’ House Bill 4121 (2024)” (search result, https://www.oregon.gov/olcc/marijuana/pages/recreational-marijuana-licensee-reports.aspx — Run 1 §4.9).
  • Change-of-ownership rule — current text Verify, draft formulation noted. A 2015 draft of the Division 25 rules (labelled “Draft Only – Do not use for business decisions”, https://www.oregon.gov/olcc/marijuana/documents/draft_845_025_recreationalmarijuanadraftrules.pdf — search result, accessed 2026-11-01) states: “(2) Change of Ownership. If a licensee has a change in ownership that is 51% or greater, a new application must be submitted” and “(3) Changes in Financial Interest or Business Structure. A licensee that proposes to change its corporate structure or change who has a financial interest in the business must submit a form prescribed by the Commission, and any information identified in the form to be submitted, to the Commission, prior to making such a change. (a) The Commission must review the form … and will approve the change if the change would not result in an initial or renewal application denial under OAR 845-025-1115, or serve as the basis of a license suspension or revocation. (b) If the Commission denies the change but the licensee proceeds with the change the licensee must surrender the license or the Commission will propose to suspend or revoke the license.” The 51% threshold and the pre-change filing duty are stated here ONLY as the draft formulation — the current OAR 845-025-1160/1170-series (change of ownership / change of location / change of business structure) text was NOT opened in this run (rate-limit) and must be confirmed before advising any transaction. Do not quote 51% as current law from this draft alone. The same formulation appears in a 2018 OLCC bill-package draft (https://www.oregon.gov/olcc/marijuana/Documents/Rules/2018_BillPackage/2018_MJBill%20TechPackage_Draft.pdf — search result, accessed 2026-11-01), which corroborates the formulation’s lineage but not its currency.
  • What a change-of-ownership approval does NOT promise. Cold Frame settlement (secondary, accessed 2026-11-01): “The commission makes no promise that a new owner will be licensed by that date or at all. Any new owner must complete the full application process and win final commission approval.” — https://www.cannabisnews.org/united-states-cannabis-news/oregon-olcc-cold-frame-kief-lab-samples-thc-potency-license-surrender/ — secondary. A purchase agreement should therefore not treat OLCC approval as automatic or timed.
  • Tax-compliance gate on transfer/renewal (retailers). Run 1 §4.10 (secondary, CannBus Q3 2026, citing OLCC practice): retailers must show a certificate of tax compliance to renew or transfer; the underlying rule (retailers current on taxes or on a qualifying payment plan before renewal, adopted 2023, upheld by the Oregon Court of Appeals in 2025) is Verify in current OAR 845-025. ORS 475C.265 retailer tax-nonpayment revocation (Run 1 §1.2.2): the Commission “may revoke a marijuana retailer license … if the licensee fails to: (A) Pay the tax as required under ORS 475C.682 … twice in any four consecutive quarters and the Department of Revenue has issued … a distraint warrant under ORS 475C.688” — verbatim excerpt, Run 1.
  • LUCS on changes. Adding a processor endorsement (concentrate/edible/topical/extract) requires OLCC approval and a LUCS showing the endorsement is not a prohibited use (new LUCS not required if only adding the industrial-hemp endorsement) — Run 1 §4.4 (legacy form-derived — Verify current CAMP form). Change-of-location generally requires a new LUCS and local review; the $1,000 location-transfer fee is Run 1 §4.2 (OLCC fee page, opened in Run 1).

11.2.2 Renewal — requirements and timelines

  • Annual renewal (OLCC licences, including labs). OAR 845-025-5030(3)(a) (opened): “A laboratory must renew its license annually and pay the required renewal fees in accordance with OAR 845-025-1190 (License Renewal).” — https://oregon.public.law/rules/oar_845-025-5030 — accessed 2026-11-01. OAR 845-025-1190 is the general renewal rule for all OLCC licences; its full text (renewal window, late-renewal grace, expiration consequences) was NOT opened in this run (rate-limit) — Verify: do not state a renewal window (e.g. 30/60/90 days before expiry) or a late fee from this draft. Renewal application fee $250 non-refundable + licence fee = same as initial licence fee (Run 1 §4.2, OLCC fee page opened in Run 1).
  • Renewal investigation. A 2018 draft formulation (search result, accessed 2026-11-01) states: “The Commission may require submission of forms, documents and information described in OAR 845-025-1030 in order to complete an investigation of a renewal application. Failure to submit forms, documents or information requested … within a reasonable period of time as determined by the Commission may result in denial of the renewal application and revocation of the license.” — https://www.oregon.gov/olcc/marijuana/Documents/Rules/2018_BillPackage/2018_MJBill%20TechPackage_Draft.pdf — draft formulation only — Verify against current OAR 845-025-1190.
  • Renewal denial grounds. Lab renewal “may be denied for any violation of [ORS 475C.540–475C.590], OAR 333-007-0300 to 333-007-0490, OAR 333, Division 64, or these rules” — OAR 845-025-5030(3)(b) (opened). General renewal denial grounds are in OAR 845-025-1115 (Denial of Application) — not opened — Verify.
  • Research certificate term: 3 years ($4,750 for the term — Run 1 §4.2). Worker permit term: 5 years ($100 — Run 1 §4.2, §11.8). ODA hemp licences: 1 year, 1 Jan–31 Dec; renewal + full fee by 1 Dec of the current year; no new grow sites after 31 May (31 July with $250 late fee) — Run 1 §4.8 (ODA applications rev. 11/2025 and 9/2026).
  • Medical (OMMP) renewals: patient cards, grow-site registrations and processing-site registrations renew under OAR 333 Div. 8; grow-site registration fee $200 except $0 where the patient grows for self at own residence with ≤12 mature plants and no transfer to a dispensary/processing site (Run 1 §4.7, OHA form instructions Dec 2025). Current OMMP renewal windows/fees are Verify on the OHA/OMMP pages — the Dec 2025 form is the latest form located, not a confirmed 2026 fee schedule.

11.2.3 Ownership caps, multiple licences, financial interest

  • No Oregon ownership cap confirmed. Run 1 §4.10: “No current Oregon ownership cap (e.g. a maximum number of licences per person) was confirmed on an opened official page in this run. MPP (secondary) reports OLCC ‘tightened transfer restrictions to curb license speculation and consolidation’ in 2025” — https://www.mpp.org/states/oregon/ — accessed 2026-11-01 in Run 1. Part 11 confirms: no cap figure was located on an opened official page in this run either. Ownership caps, vertical-integration limits, and financial-interest disclosure rules remain Verify — they belong in current OAR 845-025-1030/1115/1160-series text, not assumed here.
  • Financial-interest review (draft formulation, lineage corroborated). A 2015-era Division 25 text (search result, accessed 2026-11-01) states: “The Commission may refuse to issue a license to any license applicant or refuse to renew the license of any licensee when conditions exist in relation to any person having a financial interest in the business or in the place of business which would constitute grounds for refusing to issue a license or for revocation or suspension of a license if such person were the license applicant or licensee. However, in cases where the financial interest is held by a corporation, only the officers and directors of the corporation, any individual or combination of individuals who own a controlling financial interest in the business shall be considered persons having a financial interest” — https://www.oregon.gov/olcc/marijuana/Documents/TemporaryMarijuanaRules_adopted_121815.pdf — 2015 temporary-rules text — Verify current OAR 845-025-1015/1115 definitions of “financial interest” and “controlling interest” before advising.
  • Multiple licence types per person: Run 1 §4.3 (secondary, League of Oregon Cities Municipal Handbook ch. 27, May 2021, updated Oct 2025): “A person may hold more than one licence type, subject to OLCC rules” — https://www.orcities.org/application/files/3117/6851/9196/Municipal_Handbook_-Chapter_27-_Marijuana.pdf — accessed 2026-11-01 in Run 1. Verify the current multiple-licence / financial-interest rules in OAR 845-025 before relying on them. The lab bar (§11.1.6) is the one hard single-licence-type exclusion confirmed in rule text.
  • Residency: Run 1 §4.10 left residency Verify (litigation + legislative change; secondary sources conflict). Part 11 leaves it Verify — do not advise any applicant on residency until current ORS 475C / OAR 845-025 text and pending litigation are checked.

11.2.4 Relocation (change of location)

  • Fee: $1,000 per licence (Run 1 §4.2, OLCC fee page opened in Run 1).
  • Operating at the new location BEFORE approval is a violation: Feb 2026 stipulated settlement (Portland Canna / Hawthco One Corporation, OLCC SSA Feb 2026, search result, accessed 2026-11-01): licensee “engaged in activities that require a license at the Unlicensed Location prior to the Commission approving the change of location request, when Licensee began operating at the Unlicensed Location, including engaging in sales” (OAR 845-025-1180(5) charge, 2nd-level Category I in the settlement’s characterisation) and “dismantled surveillance equipment at the licensed location and continued to transact sales at the licensed location without surveillance cameras” — https://www.oregon.gov/olcc/Docs/stipulated_settlements/marijuana/SSA-February-2026-MJ.pdf — accessed 2026-11-01. Settlement terms included surrender/destruction of items at the unlicensed premises (or destruction with OLCC inspectors present) and maintaining security/surveillance there while items remained — same source.
  • Current change-of-location rule number, LUCS requirement, local-government notice, and processing timeline were NOT opened in this run — Verify in current OAR 845-025-1180 and the CAMP change-of-location form. The Feb 2026 settlement also shows OLCC will process a renewal alongside a change-of-ownership where the licensee lost access to the premises, and will not deny renewal solely on OAR 845-025-1115(2)(h) lack-of-access grounds in that settlement’s terms — settlement-specific, do not generalise.

11.2.5 Surrender

  • Voluntary surrender by agreement: Cold Frame (§11.1.7) — surrender by 7 a.m. 13 Jan 2027 unless change-of-ownership approved; “The OLCC may seize and destroy any marijuana items still on the formerly licensed premises, or still in the company’s METRC tracking inventory, after the surrender” (secondary, accessed 2026-11-01).
  • Surrender as a settlement term for unlicensed-location items: Portland Canna Feb 2026 settlement — items at the unlicensed premises to be “surrendered to OLCC for destruction or destroyed with OLCC inspectors present” — same SSA source.
  • Surrender of a failed-test batch: §11.1.5 — licensee may elect to surrender failed pesticide/solvent items to Commission staff for destruction (form summary).
  • Surrender of an endorsement: processor endorsement surrender requires written notice with the cessation date (Run 1 §4.4, legacy form — Verify current form).
  • Surrender of OHA registration on OLCC licensure: “OLCC will not issue a licence to a site registered with OHA for medical production; any OHA registration for the site must be surrendered at licensure” (Run 1 §4.3, OLCC medically-designated-canopy form instructions).
  • General surrender procedure (form, notice period, inventory disposition, tax clearance on surrender) was NOT located on an opened official page in this run — Verify in OAR 845-025-1190/1250-series and the CAMP surrender form before advising a surrender.

11.2.6 Revocation, suspension, restriction — grounds and penalty categories

  • Statutory grounds — ORS 475C.265 (Run 1 §1.2.2, verbatim excerpt): the Commission “may revoke, suspend or restrict a license issued under ORS 475C.005 … to 475C.525 … or 475C.548 … or require a licensee or licensee representative to undergo training if the commission finds or has reasonable ground to believe that the licensee or licensee representative: (a) Has violated a provision of ORS 475C.005 … to 475C.525 … or 475C.540 … to 475C.586 … or a rule adopted under [those sections]; (b) Has diverted marijuana to the interstate market or an illicit market or has diverted resources to a criminal enterprise. … [Has] introduced into the marijuana industry regulated under [ORS 475C] cannabinoids or marijuana not produced or processed by a licensee and not tracked in the system developed and maintained under ORS 475C.177 … [Has] made any false representation or statement to the commission regarding compliance … in order to induce or prevent action by the commission. (e) Is in the habit of using alcoholic liquor, habit-forming drugs, marijuana or controlled substances to excess. … [Has] misrepresented to a customer or the public any marijuana items sold by the licensee or licensee representative.” — https://oregon.public.law/statutes/ors_475c.265 — Run 1. History not returned for 475C.265 — Verify last amendment on the official ORS page.
  • Penalty categories (OAR 845-025-8500 series, as characterised in enforcement documents): Category I = most serious, default sanction revocation/cancellation (e.g. potency misrepresentation OAR 845-025-8540(2)(a)(C); testing-rule violation OAR 845-025-5700(3); unaccredited lab activity OAR 845-025-5030(2)(f)); Category II = e.g. failure to submit audit samples (OAR 845-025-5760(6)); lower categories carry suspension/fines with mitigation/aggravation. The full penalty schedule (OAR 845-025-8525/8540/8550 etc., fine amounts, suspension-day ranges, Category I–IV definitions) was NOT opened in this run — Verify against current OAR before quoting any fine or suspension figure. Do not quote a dollar fine from secondary enforcement reporting as the schedule amount.
  • 2026 revocation/suspension context: seven-lab notices 25 Sep 2026 (proposed cancellation in some cases, suspension/fines in others — Run 1 H5); Cold Frame surrender-in-lieu (15 Oct 2026); Portland Canna Feb 2026 settlement (camera dismantling, unlicensed-location operation — proposed penalty in the notice was licence cancellation for the camera counts, per the SSA summary). Final dispositions for the seven labs are Unavailable in this run — Verify on OLCC commission orders.
  • Training as an alternative/additional sanction: ORS 475C.265 allows the Commission to “require a licensee or licensee representative to undergo training” instead of or in addition to revocation/suspension/restriction (Run 1 excerpt).

11.2.7 Licence terms, caps, and what is NOT capped

  • HB 4121 caps (operative 1 Jan 2025): 1 producer/retailer per 7,500 residents 21+; 1 processor/wholesaler per 12,500 residents 21+. Caps do NOT apply to renewal applications or to new licences resulting from a change in location or ownership (Run 1 §4.9).
  • “HB 4121 per-capita caps (no calendar sunset)” conflict (carried from Run 1 §4.9/§4.13): some secondary sources describe the moratorium as “extended until at least HB 4121 per-capita caps (no calendar sunset)”; HB 4121’s structure is a permanent cap system from 2025, not a HB 4121 per-capita caps (no calendar sunset) sunset. Unresolved in this run — Verify on OLIS whether any 2025 bill re-imposed a HB 4121 per-capita caps (no calendar sunset) date.
  • Wholesale lift: RAC call closed 28 Aug 2026, RAC met 25 Sep 2026, staff concluded active wholesale licences had fallen below the cap; wholesale applications remain closed until rules are adopted (Run 1 §4.9; secondary: https://www.cannabisnews.org/united-states-cannabis-news/oregon-starts-rulemaking-that-could-lift-cannabis-wholesale-license-moratorium/ (29 Aug 2026) and https://themarijuanaherald.com/2026/08/oregon-begins-rulemaking-process-that-could-lift-marijuana-wholesale-license-moratorium-for-first-time-since-2022/ (28 Aug 2026) — both accessed 2026-11-01 in Run 1). Verify current RAC/rulemaking status on the OLCC rulemaking page.
  • NOT stated to be capped (Verify each, Run 1 §4.9): laboratory, sampling laboratory, research certificate, hemp certificate, worker permits, ODA hemp licences. Do not assume closed; do not assume open without checking CAMP/ODA.

11.2.8 Insurance and bonding — GAP REPORTED, NOT FILLED

  • No general OLCC insurance minimum (e.g. general liability, product liability, crop) and no surety-bond minimum for OLCC licensees was located in the OAR 845-025 material returned in this run. No bonding figure appears in the Run 1 fee schedule (§4.2) or in the OLCC premises/security checklists returned.
  • What IS required instead (and must not be mislabelled as insurance): a security plan (§11.4); locked storage; Metrc tracking; tax compliance; and, for specific activities, third-party certifications (e.g. child-resistant package certification by a qualified third-party testing firm under OAR 845-025-7160(2)(a)(A) — Run 1 §1.6.1; hydrocarbon extraction equipment inspection by a certified engineer/third party/manufacturer — Run 1 §4.4).
  • Related requirements that are NOT an OLCC bond: ODA food-establishment licensing for edible processors (Run 1 §4.4); local-government LUCS/permits; landlord insurance covenants (private contract, not OLCC rule); workers’ compensation under general Oregon employment law (not a cannabis rule — Verify with BOLI/DCBS before advising).
  • Action: Verify by searching current OAR 845-025-1030 (application contents) and 845-025-1200-series for any insurance/bonding paragraph, and the CAMP application checklist, before stating “Oregon requires no insurance/bond” as a definitive negative. This draft states only that none was located.

11.3 Cultivation rules

11.3.1 Producer canopy tiers — indoor / outdoor / mixed (Run 1 §4.3, carried as snippet-derived)

From OAR 845-025-2040 as rendered in search results in Run 1 (direct open failed in Run 1 — snippet-derived, Verify): https://oregon.public.law/rules/oar_845-025-2040 — accessed 2026-11-01 in Run 1.

Tier Indoor mature canopy Outdoor mature canopy
Micro Tier I Up to 625 sq ft Up to 2,500 sq ft
Micro Tier II 626–1,250 sq ft 2,501–5,000 sq ft
Tier I 1,251–5,000 sq ft 5,001–20,000 sq ft
Tier II 5,001–10,000 sq ft 20,001–40,000 sq ft
  • Mixed production = growing both indoors and outdoors at the same licensed premises; the Commission uses a 4:1 ratio (outdoor:indoor) to allocate canopy, not to exceed the sum limits above (Run 1 §4.3).
  • Immature canopy limits for licences issued/renewed after 1 Apr 2018 (snippet-derived, Verify): Micro I 625 sq ft; Micro II 1,250 sq ft; Tier I 5,000 sq ft; Tier II 10,000 sq ft (Run 1 §4.3).
  • A producer must document size, method, measurements and shapes for each canopy area; a mature plant may only be in a designated mature canopy area; changing a canopy location/shape, producer type, method or tier needs prior written Commission approval (Run 1 §4.3). No more than 20 quadrilateral canopy areas (or 20 canopy areas of any shape under the alternative prong, text truncated in the Run 1 snippet — Verify the full paragraph).
  • Definitions (2015 draft, lineage only — Verify current OAR 845-025-2040 definitions): “Canopy means the surface area utilized to produce mature marijuana plants calculated in square feet and measured using the outside boundaries of any area that includes mature marijuana plants including all of the space within the boundaries.” “Indoor production means producing marijuana in any manner: (a) Utilizing artificial lighting on mature marijuana plants; or (b) Other than [outdoor production].” “Outdoor production means producing marijuana: (a) In an expanse of open or cleared ground; or (b) In a greenhouse, hoop house or similar non-rigid structure that does not utilize any artificial lighting on mature marijuana plants, including but not limited to electrical lighting sources.” — https://www.oregon.gov/olcc/marijuana/documents/draft_845_025_recreationalmarijuanadraftrules.pdf — draft, accessed 2026-11-01. The greenhouse/hoop-house classification matters: a hoop house WITHOUT artificial light on mature plants counts as outdoor; WITH artificial light it counts as indoor. SB 162 (2025) hoop-house provisions (Run 1 H11, status conflict — Verify on OLIS) may have changed this — do not advise on hoop houses without checking SB 162’s enrolled text and current OAR 845-025-2040.
  • Fees by tier (Run 1 §4.2): Micro I $1,000, Micro II $2,000, Tier I $3,750, Tier II $5,750 per year + $250 application.

11.3.2 Indoor / outdoor / mixed operational rules (what the tiers imply)

  • Indoor: artificial lighting on mature plants = indoor, regardless of structure. Indoor areas are subject to the full premises/security rules (§11.4), including permanent walls/doors, commercial-grade locks, steel door/frame for indoor storage areas (checklist, §11.4.1).
  • Outdoor: open/cleared ground or non-rigid structure without artificial light on mature plants. Outdoor canopy must still be within the licensed premises, secured (fencing/gates with commercial-grade locks per checklist), and not visible from a public place by normal unaided vision where the visibility rule applies (home-grow visibility rule, §11.3.3; licensed-premises visibility — Verify the licensed-premises visibility rule in OAR 845-025-1230/1400-series, not assumed from the home-grow rule).
  • Mixed: 4:1 outdoor:indoor allocation (Run 1 §4.3). The arithmetic of mixed allocation (whether the 4:1 ratio caps the combined canopy at the tier maximum or allows indoor + outdoor up to their separate maxima) was not confirmed on an opened rule page — Verify with a worked example in OAR 845-025-2040 before calculating a mixed canopy.
  • Micro-tier processing privilege: Micro Tier I/II producers may hold a micro-tier processing endorsement (concentrate only, per Run 1 §4.3 Portland-code summary — Verify current endorsement list in OAR 845-025).
  • Medically designated canopy (producer privilege): up to 10% of the tier’s maximum mature canopy IN ADDITION to the licensed canopy (e.g. Tier II outdoor: up to 4,000 sq ft in addition to 40,000 sq ft; Micro I indoor: up to 62.5 sq ft in addition to 625 sq ft), provided at least 75% of the annual yield from the medically designated canopy is provided to OMMP cardholders for no consideration. Fee $100 in the OAR 845-025-1060 snippet (Verify). A producer may transfer immature plants to a PRMG at the PRMG’s grow site, or to a cardholder/caregiver at the producer’s premises, under OAR 845-025-2550. OLCC will not issue a licence to a site registered with OHA for medical production; OHA registration must be surrendered at licensure (Run 1 §4.3, OLCC form https://www.oregon.gov/olcc/marijuana/Documents/Licensing_Forms/mj_opt_pro_medcanopy.pdf).

11.3.3 OMMP grow-site limits (medical regime — distinct from home grow)

  • Per-patient plant limits (secondary, Safe Access Now, accessed 2026-11-01 in Run 1): per registered patient, a grow site may produce up to 6 mature plants, 12 immature plants 24 inches or more in height, and 36 immature plants less than 24 inches in height. Verify against OAR 333-008-0500-series before quoting as law.
  • Grower cap: a designated grower (PRMG) must be 21+ and may grow for no more than eight registered patients at one time [corrected on audit from four — OAR 333-008-0550(1)], subject to OMMP criminal-history check (Run 1 §4.7).
  • Residence cap: where the grow site is the patient’s residence and the patient (or that patient’s caregiver) is the designated grower, no more than 12 mature plants if more than two patients are registered to the site (OHA change-form instructions, Dec 2025, http://egov.oregon.gov/oha/PH/DISEASESCONDITIONS/CHRONICDISEASE/MEDICALMARIJUANAPROGRAM/Documents/form/Change_form_and_Instructions_12-16-25.pdf — Run 1 §4.7).
  • Grow-site fee: $200, paid by the grower, except $0 where the patient grows for self at own residence with ≤12 mature plants and will not transfer to an OMMP dispensary/processing site; $200 is triggered if the grower is not also the patient, the site is not the patient’s residence, the site has >12 mature plants, or the grower transfers to a dispensary/processing site (same OHA form instructions).
  • Property-owner consent from 1 Jan 2026: where the patient/grower does not own the property, a notarised Medical Marijuana Grow Site Consent form from the property owner is required (SB 907, 2025 session, per secondary summary in Run 1 §4.7 — Verify bill and OAR text).
  • Zoning/physical-address rules: proof of zoning required if the grow site address is within city limits; a grow site must have a physical Oregon address and must not be located at a medical or retail marijuana dispensary (legacy OHA form statements in Run 1 §4.7 — Verify current OAR 333-008).
  • Reporting/tracking by patient count: grow sites with 3+ patients must track in CTS/Metrc, designate a Grow Site Administrator, and pay the CTS user fee within 15 days of OMMP notification (older checklist: $480 CTS user fee to OMMP — Verify current fee; may be stale); sites with ≤2 patients report monthly in OMMOS if a trigger applies (transfers, non-residence self-grow, etc.), by the 10th of each month for the previous month (OAR 333-008-0630, Run 1 §1.7). Exempt from both only if: patient growing only for self at own residence + ≤2 patients at the site + no transfer to a processing site/dispensary indicated (Run 1 §1.7).
  • Grandfather petitions under OAR 333-008-0520 exist for certain grow-site addresses (legacy form reference in Run 1 §4.7 — Verify current availability).
  • Grow-site counts (conflict carried from Run 1 §4.7/§5.5): CannBus restatement of the July 2026 OHA snapshot: growers 2,289, grow sites 2,101; the snapshot PDF’s grow-site-address table totals 2,723 on p. 4 as rendered. Do not quote either without noting the conflict until the snapshot PDF is opened in full. Grow sites with 3+ patients fell from ~4,200 to ~150 (advocacy secondary, Compassionate Oregon — Verify against OHA snapshots).

11.3.4 Home grow — reconciliation with Run 1 (no contradiction)

  • 4 plants per household at any time, regardless of how many adults live there (ORS 475C.305(1) as summarised in Brown v. City of Grants Pass, Run 1 §1.1/§1.3.2). This draft does not change that figure.
  • Visibility: plants/products must not be visible from a public place by normal unaided vision (Run 1 §1.1).
  • Home-grow possession caps sit alongside, not instead of, the plant cap: up to 8 oz usable marijuana at home for 21+ (ORS 475C.337(1)(c)), 2 oz in public (475C.337(1)(b)) — Run 1 §1.1/§1.3.1. Harvest from 4 plants may exceed 8 oz; the possession cap, not the plant cap, governs what may be kept — Verify the harvest/possession interaction in ORS 475C.337 before advising a home grower on excess harvest (Run 1 flagged this interaction only implicitly; it is not resolved by the plant rule alone).
  • Home grow vs OMMP grow site vs licensed producer — three regimes, do not conflate: (1) Home grow: 4 plants/household, 21+, no licence/registration, no sale. (2) OMMP grow site: per-patient limits (§11.3.3), OHA registration, may supply cardholders. (3) OLCC producer: canopy tiers (§11.3.1), OLCC licence, commercial sale to licensees only. A person may be in more than one regime only as the rules allow (e.g. OLCC licensure requires surrender of OHA registration for the same site — §11.3.2).
  • Local rules: home grow is subject to local zoning/nuisance rules (Part 3 territory) and to lease restrictions (private contract, Run 1 §1.1). No OLCC worker permit is required for personal home grow (worker permits are for licensee/laboratory work — §11.8).

11.3.5 Hemp cultivation (ODA — operations cross-reference)

  • ODA grower $350 + grow site $875 + $75/key participant; licence year 1 Jan–31 Dec; renewal + full fee by 1 Dec; no new grow sites after 31 May (31 July with $250 late fee); fees non-refundable, not prorated (Run 1 §4.8, ODA grower application rev. 11/2025).
  • Growers must register the grow site with the USDA Farm Service Agency (FSA) (same application).
  • Pre-harvest THC testing, sampling, and destruction of hot crops are ODA/USDA-plan rules (Part 7 territory for full treatment; §11.1.8 for the testing cross-reference). Hemp canopy tiers do NOT exist in the OLCC sense — ODA hemp has no Micro/Tier I/Tier II canopy system; do not apply §11.3.1 tiers to hemp.

11.4 Security

11.4.1 Premises security — locks, walls, storage (OAR 845-025-1400–1470 series)

Rule numbers in this section are from the OLCC premises requirements checklist and the Lake Oswego code summary (which lists the series as OAR 845-025-1400 through 845-025-1470). Individual rule texts in the 1400-series were NOT opened in this run (rate-limit) — each proposition below is checklist-derived or secondary-derived and must be verified against the SOS OAR page before advising on a build-out.

  • Security plan required at application: premises sketch/floor plans must match the physical location, and the applicant/licensee must have a security plan (OLCC premises checklist, Form MJ 23-1405 rev. 20231114, https://stage.oregon.gov/olcc/marijuana/Documents/Licensing_Forms/mj_ref_all_lic_premises_requirements.pdf — search result, accessed 2026-11-01). Lake Oswego code summary (secondary, municipal code restating OLCC rules): facilities “shall comply with … security regulations (OAR 845-025-1400 through 845-025-1470)” — https://ecode360.com/43165577 — accessed 2026-11-01.
  • Enclosure and locks (checklist, OAR 845-025-1410 as cited on the checklist): “Entire premises is enclosed by permanent walls & doors” (processor inspection checklist, https://data.templateroller.com/pdf_docs/2284/22840/2284082/main_marijuana-processor-inspection-checklist-oregon.pdf — search result, accessed 2026-11-01); “Exterior entries secured by nonresidential commercial-grade locks”; “Areas where marijuana items will be stored are locked, indoor areas secured with a properly installed steel door with a steel frame, and a commercial grade lock” (retailers subject to separate requirements — checklist note); “When closed, facility is securely locked and keys/codes remain only with [authorised persons]” (checklist, truncated in return — Verify full text).
  • No subletting: “A licensee may not sublet any portion of the premises” (processor checklist, OAR 845-025-1230 as cited — Verify current rule number).
  • Limited Access Areas: cameras must cover “all Limited Access Areas including all buildings, rooms, or other contiguous areas on a licensed premises where a marijuana item is present” (premises checklist, OAR 845-025-1440 as cited). Access to Limited Access Areas is restricted to licensees, worker-permit holders, and authorised visitors under escort rules — the visitor/escort rule text was not opened — Verify in OAR 845-025-1230/1400-series.
  • Theft notification: licensee must notify the Commission “as soon as reasonably practical and in no case more than 24 hours from the theft of marijuana items or money from the licensed premises” (2015 temporary-rules text, https://www.oregon.gov/olcc/marijuana/Documents/TemporaryMarijuanaRules_adopted_121815.pdf — search result, accessed 2026-11-01). 2015 text — Verify current OAR 845-025-1400-series theft/loss notification rule (including loss, not just theft, and Metrc inventory-adjustment duties).
  • Retailer signage (Run 1 §1.6.2, OAR 845-025-2840(2)): prominent signs: “No Minors Permitted Anywhere on the Premises”; “No On-Site Consumption”; “Security Cameras in Use”; plus exit sign: “Marijuana or Marijuana Infused Products May Not Be Consumed In Public.”
  • Cash storage (local overlay, NOT a statewide OLCC rule as returned): Lake Oswego code requires retailers/wholesalers to “maintain a safe drop-box for storage of cash receipts” (a locking receptacle affixed to the building) — https://ecode360.com/43165577 — municipal code, not OLCC rule; do not present as statewide. Whether OLCC requires a safe/vault statewide is Verify in OAR 845-025-1400-series (secondary vendor summaries assert a “safe vault” — see §11.4.1 note below).
  • Vendor restatement (secondary, use with caution): Safe and Sound Security (vendor site, accessed 2026-11-01): “A compliant Oregon cannabis security system has to include: Continuous 24/7 video recording wherever marijuana items are present, plus every point of entry and exit. Minimum resolution of 720p (1280 by 720), recording at a minimum of 10 frames per second wherever camera coverage is required. Camera coverage that captures clear images within 15 feet inside and outside every entrance, and covers all limited-access areas, point-of-sale areas, and the surveillance room. Recordings kept for a minimum of 90 calendar days, with off-site backup of the surveillance room’s footage. A failure-notification system that alerts staff within one hour of any interruption, and written notice to the OLCC for outages of 30 minutes or more.” — https://getsafeandsound.com/oregon-cannabis-security/ — secondary vendor summary, NOT rule text. The 720p/10fps/15-ft/90-day elements are consistent with the OLCC checklist (below) but the 1-hour alert / 30-minute OLCC-notice thresholds are vendor-stated only — Verify against OAR 845-025-1450 before quoting them.

11.4.2 Alarms and intrusion notification (OAR 845-025-1420 as cited on checklists)

  • Ability to notify law enforcement/security company on unauthorised entry: checklist requires “Ability to notify law enforcement or a security company upon any unauthorized entry” by at least one of: “Two mounted panic buttons linked with the alarm system that notifies a security company or law enforcement” (processor checklist, OAR 845-025-1420 as cited) — or an alternative mechanism where a licensee representative is physically present at all times when closed (checklist alternative, OAR 845-025-1420). The checklist also states: “The applicant/licensee must still have a mechanism to ensure that the licensee, employees, and representatives can immediately notify law enforcement of any unauthorized entry (OAR 845-025-1420)” even under the present-representative alternative.
  • No statewide “guard required” rule was located. Secondary vendor summary: “Oregon does not require on-site guards at every cannabis business, but operators hire them for after-hours deterrence, front-door ID checks, and control of the inventory room.” — https://getsafeandsound.com/oregon-cannabis-security/ — secondary. Verify: if any licence type or local jurisdiction requires guards, it is not in the OLCC checklist material returned.
  • Alarm-system failure notification thresholds (1 hour / 30 minutes) are vendor-stated only — see §11.4.1. Verify in OAR 845-025-1450.

11.4.3 Cameras and video retention (OAR 845-025-1440/1450 as cited on checklists)

  • Coverage (checklist, OAR 845-025-1440): “Cameras are placed to capture clear and certain images of any individual and activity occurring within 15’ both inside and outside of all points of ingress and egress to and from the licensed premises” (processor checklist); “Cameras cover all Limited Access Areas” and “Camera(s) cover all surveillance area(s) or surveillance room(s) and individuals accessing [them]” (premises checklist). Draft-rule formulation (2015, lineage only): “A licensed premises must have camera coverage, as applicable, for: (a) All limited access areas …; (b) All point of sale areas; (c) All points of entry to or exit from limited access areas; and (d) All points of entry to or exit from the licensed premises; (2) A licensee must ensure that cameras are placed so that they capture clear and certain images of any individual and activity occurring: (a) Within 15 feet both inside and outside of all points of entry to and exit from the licensed premises; and (b) Anywhere within secure or limited access areas” — https://www.oregon.gov/olcc/marijuana/documents/draft_845_025_recreationalmarijuanadraftrules.pdf — draft, accessed 2026-11-01.
  • Recording (checklist, OAR 845-025-1450): “Accurate date and time stamp embedded on video without obscuring image”; “All cameras continuously record, 24 hours a day, and in the absence of visible light” (premises checklist).
  • Retention (checklist, OAR 845-025-1450): “Licensee has kept a minimum of 90 calendar days of surveillance recordings on-site” and “Licensee has kept a minimum of 30 days of off-site backup recordings stored off-site” (premises checklist, Form MJ 23-1405 rev. 20231114). The 90-day on-site figure is checklist-confirmed; the 30-day off-site figure is checklist-derived and the vendor summary phrases it as “off-site backup of the surveillance room’s footage” without a day count — Verify the off-site retention period and scope (all footage vs surveillance-room footage only) against OAR 845-025-1450 text.
  • Resolution/frame rate (vendor-stated, Verify): 720p minimum, 10 fps minimum (vendor summary, §11.4.1). The checklist does not state resolution/fps in the excerpts returned — Verify in OAR 845-025-1450.
  • Enforcement illustration: Portland Canna Feb 2026 settlement — licensee “dismantled surveillance equipment at the licensed location and continued to transact sales at the licensed location without surveillance cameras” (OAR 845-025-1440/1450 charges; proposed penalty licence cancellation for the camera counts) — https://www.oregon.gov/olcc/Docs/stipulated_settlements/marijuana/SSA-February-2026-MJ.pdf — accessed 2026-11-01. Operating without cameras is treated as a top-tier violation, not a paperwork lapse.
  • Security waiver: processor checklist includes an “Approved Security Waiver? ☐ No ☐ Yes” field — the waiver rule (grounds, scope, duration) was not opened — Verify in OAR 845-025-1400-series / OLCC waiver guidance before advising any applicant to seek one.

11.4.4 Transport and delivery vehicles

  • Licensee-to-licensee transport (OAR 845-025-7700): processor checklist: “Vehicles for transport must be alarmed, secure marijuana out of sight” (OAR 845-025-7700 as cited); “When transferring inventory, must do so in compliance with all rules, specifically OAR 845-025-7700” — same checklist. Lake Oswego code summary lists “transportation and delivery (OAR 845-025-7700)” as a compliance series — https://ecode360.com/43165577. Full 7700 text (manifest, vehicle registration, driver permit, GPS, locked container, transfer windows) was NOT opened — Verify.
  • Retail delivery to consumers (ORS 475C.117, verbatim excerpts, Run 1 §1.6.3): retailer may deliver pursuant to a bona fide order (a) within the same city/unincorporated county area, or (b) into an adjacent city/county area ONLY if that adjacent jurisdiction has adopted a delivery opt-in ordinance; retailer must on request provide vehicle information (make, model, year, color, VIN, plate); delivery individual must hold an ORS 475C.273 worker permit and carry it, present a printed/electronic delivery manifest and obtain the consumer’s written/electronic signature verifying completion, travel only between the retailer’s premises and delivery locations except for emergency/unsafe roads/fuel/rest/repair, and may NOT: leave a delivery vehicle containing marijuana items unattended unless locked and equipped with an active vehicle alarm; carry more than $10,000 worth of marijuana items at any one time; consume or be under the influence of marijuana while delivering. Delivery vehicle must: have an active GPS device tracking location and enabling the retailer to identify it; have a lockable container in a secured cargo area of appropriate size; be free of markings indicating it delivers marijuana items. No delivery to a consumer on federal land. — https://oregon.public.law/statutes/ors_475C.117 ; history “[2021 c.155 §3]” — Run 1.
  • Delivery hours/frequency (secondary, Verify): deliveries 8:00 a.m.–9:00 p.m.; one delivery per address per day; daily sale limits apply equally to delivery and in-person sales (Run 1 §1.6.3, secondary FAQ summary — Verify rule citation OAR 845-025-2800-series/delivery rule). Retailer store hours generally (7 a.m.–10 p.m. in one secondary summary) are likewise Verify.
  • Metrc transfer duties: all licensee-to-licensee transfers must be recorded in CTS/Metrc (Run 1 §1.7); introducing untracked product is an ORS 475C.265 revocation ground.
  • Hemp transport: hemp items move under ODA/OLCC hemp rules, NOT Metrc (HB 4121 repealed the ODA hemp-tracking rulemaking duty — Run 1 §1.7). Hemp transport manifest/vehicle rules, if any, are Verify in OAR 603 Div. 48 / 845 Div. 26.

11.4.5 Storage (general)

  • Pre-tested storage: quarantine, labelled “PRODUCT NOT TESTED” in bold capitals ≥12 pt, secured against tampering/transfer/sale until results report (OAR 845-025-5720, §11.1.4).
  • Failed-test storage: held until destroyed in an approved manner / surrendered (OAR 845-025-5740 / 333-007-0450, §11.1.5).
  • General storage: locked areas, steel door/frame + commercial-grade lock for indoor storage (checklist, §11.4.1); retailers subject to separate storage requirements (checklist note — Verify OAR 845-025-2800-series retailer storage rule).
  • Waste storage: secured waste receptacle in the licensee’s possession/control (Lake Oswego code summary, §11.5).
  • Vehicle storage: lockable container in a secured cargo area (delivery, §11.4.4); transport vehicles alarmed, product out of sight (7700, §11.4.4).

11.5 Waste disposal rules

  • Rule citation and text (Cornell LII mirror rendering, search result, accessed 2026-11-01): OAR 845-025-7750 (Waste Management) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/oregon/Or-Admin-Code-SS-845-025-7750 — snippet-derived — Verify against the SOS OAR page, but the rule’s operative structure is now stated, not merely flagged: “(1) A licensee must: (a) Store, manage and dispose of solid and liquid wastes generated during marijuana production and processing in accordance with applicable state and local laws and regulations which may include but are not limited to: (A) Solid waste requirements in ORS 459 and OAR 340 Divisions 93 to 96; (B) Hazardous waste requirements in ORS 466 and OAR 340, Divisions 100 to 106; and (C) Wastewater requirements in ORS 468B and OAR 340, Divisions 41 to 42, 44 to 45, 53, 55 and 73. (b) Store marijuana waste in a secured waste receptacle in the possession of and under the control of the licensee. (c) If a licensee generates the waste post-harvest or if an entire marijuana plant greater than 24 inches tall is designated as waste: (A) The waste must be held on the licensed premises for at least three business days under camera coverage prior to disposal. (B) The licensee must document a reason for the waste in a form and manner prescribed by the Commission. (C) The licensee must document the exact time and method of destruction in a form and manner prescribed by the Commission. (d) For waste that was previously designated a marijuana item, all licensees must: (A) Hold on the licensed premises for at least three business days under camera coverage prior to disposal; (B) Document a reason for the waste …; and (C) Document the exact time and method of destruction … (2) A licensee may give or sell marijuana waste to a producer, processor or wholesale licensee or research certificate holder. Any such transaction must be entered into CTS pursuant to OAR 845-025-7500. (3) In addition to information required to be entered into CTS pursuant to OAR 845-025-7500, a licensee must maintain accurate and comprehensive records regarding waste material that accounts for, reconciles, and evidences all waste activity related to the disposal of marijuana. (4) Waste items consisting of usable marijuana, concentrates, extracts or cannabinoid products must be disposed of on the licensed premises or transferred to another licensee for disposal. (5) Any product containing marijuana or hemp waste may not be transferred or sold to any licensee for consumption.” History as rendered: OLCC 3-2015 (Temp) through OLCC 202-2022, amend filed 11/21/2022, effective 1/1/2023; Statutory authority ORS 475C.017 & 475C.117. Camera coverage for waste areas is also a security rule: OAR 845-025-1440(1)(g) (draft reclassification package, search result) requires camera coverage for “All areas where marijuana waste is required to be stored, destroyed or rendered unusable as required by OAR 845-025-7750” — https://www.oregon.gov/olcc/Docs/rules/OLCC-MJ-Violation-Reclassification-Draft.pdf — draft package, accessed 2026-11-01; failure on (1)(g) characterised there as Category II/III, vs Category I for (1)(a)–(e) — draft characterisation, Verify current penalty classification.
  • What the returned material establishes:
  • “Marijuana waste shall be stored in a secured waste receptacle in the possession of and under the control of the OLCC licensee or OHA registrant, as applicable, and disposed of in compliance with state requirements and City regulations” (Lake Oswego code, §11.4.1 source).
  • Processor checklist: “Harvest waste or plant waste from vegetative (24 inches or taller) or ma…” (truncated in return — the checklist treats vegetative plant waste ≥24 inches as a distinct waste category; the full waste line and any rendering requirement are Verify).
  • Failed-test batches: held until destroyed in a Commission-approved manner or surrendered to Commission staff for destruction (§11.1.5) — destruction of failed product is an OLCC-directed disposal, not ordinary waste disposal.
  • Surrendered/unlicensed-location items: surrendered to OLCC for destruction or destroyed with OLCC inspectors present (§11.2.5).
  • Cold Frame post-surrender: “The OLCC may seize and destroy any marijuana items still on the formerly licensed premises, or still in the company’s METRC tracking inventory, after the surrender” (secondary, §11.2.5).
  • DEQ role — limited, and a common overstatement to avoid: Oregon DEQ marijuana regulation page (search result, accessed 2026-11-01) states in substance that DEQ does not regulate marijuana air emissions as such — the search excerpt reads: “The Oregon Department of Environmental Quality does not [regulate marijuana …] emissions” (truncated; full sentence Verify on https://www.oregon.gov/deq/Regulations/Pages/MarijuanaRegulation.aspx). Do not state that DEQ “regulates cannabis waste” generally; DEQ’s role is in solid-waste / composting / wastewater overlays where they apply to a facility as a waste generator, not as a cannabis-specific waste licensor. The DEQ marijuana page itself is the Verify source.
  • Metrc waste duties: waste must be recorded in CTS (inventory adjustments) — implied by the CTS daily-reconciliation duty (Run 1 §1.7: “any time a change occurs relating to marijuana inventory … you must reflect that change in CTS”). The specific Metrc waste-adjustment procedure (waste tags, weight recording, inspector witnessing thresholds) was not opened — Verify in the OLCC CTS guides.
  • Hemp waste: ODA hemp waste (e.g. hot-crop destruction, stalk/plant waste) is under ODA/USDA-plan rules, not OAR 845-025-7750 — Verify in OAR 603 Div. 48 (Part 7 territory).
  • Metrc waste procedure (Metrc Oregon Wiki, accessed 2026-11-01): “In Metrc, Waste is defined as marijuana or marijuana items that have been rendered unusable, including the stalks, stems and branches of the marijuana plant. Waste cannot be sold or transferred to a consumer.” / “For recreational licensees most waste must be retained on the licensed premises under camera coverage in a limited access area for 3 business days. The 3 business day retention period begins when it has been recorded as waste in Metrc. The only waste not required to be retained for 3 business days prior to disposal is waste generated from pruning a plant that is still being cultivated (e.g. cutting off fan leaves) or if a whole plant less than 24 inches tall is destroyed. This type of waste must still be rendered unusable but does not need to be retained prior to disposal.” / “As long as all rules and requirements are met, licensees may at any time waste out product that has: 1. not been tested, 2. passed testing, or 3. failed for a test other than pesticides. Product that has failed pesticide testing must be retained on the licensed premises under camera coverage in a limited access area until the OLCC issues a destruction order that details when and how the product must be destroyed. Until that time it may not be disposed of.” / “Waste that comes from a Metrc package or harvest batch must be recorded in Metrc as a package adjustment.” — https://wiki-or.metrc.com/waste — Metrc guidance, accessed 2026-11-01 (guidance, not rule text — the 3-day + pesticide-destruction-order rules corroborate OAR 845-025-7750(1)(c)/(d) and §11.1.5 above).
  • Medical destruction standard (OHA Destruction and Disposal page, search result, accessed 2026-11-01): OMMP registrants “may voluntarily destroy and dispose of culled marijuana materials, including: non-viable clones; diseased plants; pruned vegetation; expired marijuana items; and, processing wastes.” Destruction method must “(1) Compl[y] with all state and local laws (including waste disposal); and (2) Mak[e] the marijuana item undesirable, unrecognizable and unfit for human or animal use; incapable of growth or germination.” Methods: “rendered unusable by grinding (for solids) and incorporating or absorbing (for liquids) the marijuana items with other material so the resulting mixture is at least fifty percent (50%) non-marijuana waste.” Disposal “by delivery of the destroyed marijuana to an offsite solid waste processing facility, such as a municipal or regional landfill, incinerator or composting site.” Table 1: plants — mix with yard debris/wood chips/sawdust/soil/manure/vegetable grease/oils/other wastes, compost or anaerobic digester if available off-site; usable marijuana — same mixture, landfill/transfer station/incinerator if composting not available/feasible; liquid concentrate/tincture/suppository — absorb in cat litter/slack lime/soil, landfill/transfer/incinerator; solid concentrate/edible/transdermal patch — mix with soil/slack lime/garbage, landfill/transfer/incinerator; liquid extract — first determine hazardous-waste status, if not hazardous absorb as above. “The extraction process is considered an industrial process; making any waste generated an industrial waste. Generators of industrial waste must make their own determination whether their waste is a hazardous waste” (DEQ hazardous-waste assistance by county). — https://www.oregon.gov/oha/ph/diseasesconditions/chronicdisease/medicalmarijuanaprogram/pages/destruction.aspx — search result, accessed 2026-11-01. This is the OMMP/medical destruction page: the 50% non-marijuana mixture standard is stated there for medical registrants. Whether the same 50% standard applies to OLCC licensees under OAR 845-025-7750 (whose rendered text above does NOT state a percentage) is Verify — do not transfer the 50% figure to OLCC licensees without the OLCC waste fact sheet / DEQ cannabis page.
  • Enforcement illustration: May 2020 SSA (Mana Holdings/Mana Farms, producer): OAR 845-025-7750(1)(c)(A)(C) charges for failing to hold post-harvest waste on the premises for at least three business days under camera coverage and failing to document exact time/method of destruction (1st-level Category III in that settlement) — https://www.oregon.gov/olcc/docs/stipulated_settlements/marijuana/SSA_May2020_MJ.pdf — accessed 2026-11-01.
  • Remaining waste Verify items: record-retention period for waste logs (beyond the CTS + “accurate and comprehensive records” duties in 7750(2)–(3)); OLCC waste fact-sheet rendering-unusable methods for licensees (vs the OHA 50% medical standard above); any local waste ordinances beyond the Lake Oswego secured-receptacle rule.

11.6 Environmental rules

11.6.1 Water rights — the governing principle (licence ≠ water right)

  • An OLCC producer licence does NOT confer a water right. Oregon water law (ORS Chapter 537, prior appropriation: “first in time, first in right”) requires a valid water right (or a lawful exemption/permit) for irrigation water use. A producer using surface water or groundwater for irrigation without a right, or beyond its right, is subject to WRD enforcement regardless of OLCC licensure.
